---
title: "T and F are variables you can overwrite"
ref: FCT-05
categories: [Factors]
impact: silencieux
attendu: "`T` always equals `TRUE`"
versions: "All"
source: "safer-r, The R Inferno"
---

::: {.piege}
```{r}
T <- 0
isTRUE(T)
if (T) {
  "yes"
} else {
  "no"
}
```
:::

## Why

`TRUE` and `FALSE` are reserved words of the language. `T` and `F` are only variables from the {base} package, set to `TRUE` and `FALSE` for convenience. An assignment `T <- 0`, or a column named `T` inside a `with()`, masks them.

Code that writes `na.rm = T` or `if (F)` then changes meaning without any error.

## The fix

Always spell out `TRUE` and `FALSE`. They cannot be overwritten: R refuses.

::: {.piege}
```{r}
rm(T)
isTRUE(T)
TRUE <- 0
```
:::
